record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: For each positive integer p, let ω_p(B^n) denote the p-width of the unit ball and let Σ_p be a smooth embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface in B^n, with multiplicity n_p, such that ω_p(B^n) = n_p|Σ_p|. Must the family {Σ_p}_{p∈N} contain infinitely many distinct hypersurfaces? If it does, must their areas satisfy |Σ_p| → +∞ as p → ∞?

evidence.quote: for each p ∈ N, there exists a smooth embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface Σ_p in B^n and a positive integer n_p ∈ N such that (3.2) ω_p(B^n) = n_p|Σ_p|.
Open Question 3. Is {Σ_p}_{p∈N} an infinite set? If so, does |Σ_p| → +∞ as p → ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ and let $B^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the closed Euclidean unit ball. A smooth properly embedded hypersurface $\Sigma \subset B^n$ is called a free boundary minimal hypersurface if it has zero mean curvature and meets $\partial B^n$ orthogonally along $\partial \Sigma$. For each positive integer $p$, the $p$-width $\omega_p(B^n)$ is defined via Almgren–Pitts min–max theory as
$$\omega_p(B^n) = \inf_{\Phi} \sup_{x \in \mathrm{dmn}(\Phi)} \mathbf{M}(\Phi(x)),$$
where the infimum is taken over all $p$-sweepouts $\Phi$ (continuous maps from a simplicial complex into the space of mod-$2$ flat $(n-1)$-cycles in $B^n$ with boundary in $\partial B^n$, having $p$-nontrivial cohomology class), and $\mathbf{M}$ denotes mass.

It is known that for each $p \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist a smooth embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface $\Sigma_p \subset B^n$ and a positive integer $n_p$ such that
$$\omega_p(B^n) = n_p \, |\Sigma_p|,$$
where $|\Sigma_p|$ denotes the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $\Sigma_p$.

Prove or disprove:
(a) The collection $\{\Sigma_p\}_{p \in \mathbb{N}}$ contains infinitely many pairwise non-congruent (or otherwise geometrically distinct) hypersurfaces.
(b) If (a) holds, then $|\Sigma_p| \to +\infty$ as $p \to \infty$.
artifact.category_tag: Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces and min-max widths
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search did not turn up a resolution of this question. Related work establishes the existence of infinite families of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces in the unit ball (e.g., O(m)×O(n)-invariant families for m+n<8) and computes the first n widths of B^n as the area of an equatorial (n−1)-ball, but does not determine whether the min-max realizing surfaces {Σ_p} form an infinite set with areas tending to infinity. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Widths of balls and free boundary minimal submanifolds
status_evidence.snippet: The k-dimensional width of a ball in a space form is given by the area of an equatorial k-ball.
status_evidence.claim: Computes certain widths of balls but does not resolve whether {Σ_p} is infinite or whether |Σ_p|→∞.

status_evidence.title: A family of free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball
status_evidence.snippet: There exists an infinite family of mutually non-congruent free boundary minimal hypersurfaces in B^{m+n} when m+n<8.
status_evidence.claim: Infinite families of FBMS exist, but it is not shown that they realize the p-widths.
